merged.author: mateuszklysz

## Before

merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** rac1 has a dead zone on each stick axis (|byte - 0x7F| from 0x30), so the stick has a cross-shaped dead zone. Ratchet has two speeds: he runs once the stick length the game reads reaches 0.819 and walks below that, about 6x slower. On a diagonal each axis gets only 0.71 of the push, so a diagonal that stops short of the rim walks while a straight push of the same length runs. The same happens to a round stick once one reading past 1.25 has marked it square (Xbox pads reach about 1.25 on diagonals). After that, a full diagonal reads as 0.80 and Ratchet walks.

**After:** a diagonal of any length reads the same as a straight push of that length, in the stick's own direction. Straight pushes, the corners and anything inside the dead zone send the same bytes as before.

merged.title: fix(hostgen): pass floats by kind through folded wrappers on Windows
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
A call through a place of a folded wrapper used the call site's type. The runtime resolves the wrapper to the function it calls, whose type hostgen does not know. On Windows x64 an argument's position decides its register, so (float, int, int) reaching the colour tween (unsigned, unsigned, float) gave garbage colours: blue explosion debris on Batalia and in a shared particle effect.

Such calls that pass a float now go through openrac_guest_call_regs, so the callee's thunk gives each kind to its own parameters. The arguments are evaluated in the same order as before.

merged.title: fix: develop's checks (render_equivalence_vulkan, xcheck_tool on Clang 18)
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** `render_equivalence_vulkan` failed in Enhanced on Ubuntu and Fedora: `shader-variants` on against off differed (5 scenarios, 0.28% of pixels, up to 8/255). The cheaper probe light for blended static passes (#165) lived only in the static variant that `shader-variants` picks. `xcheck_tool` failed with Clang 18, which leaves struct field offsets as typed `getelementptr`.

**After:** the cheaper probe light is its own registry entry, `probe-fast-blended` (on by default, with a tolerance). When it is on, blended static passes use the static variant whatever `shader-variants` says, so `shader-variants` is byte-identical again. The picture in game does not change. xcheck folds typed offsets into bytes, so Clang 18 reads the same as 19+.

**Tested:** the checks job's Python steps, `test_xcheck.py` with Clang 18/21/22, launcher `yarn verify` and `cargo fmt`. `render_equivalence_vulkan` still needs to run on CI.

merged.author: pezzadev

Vulkan driver failures could leave recording using missing objects, retry descriptor allocation indefinitely, or wait on a fence after a rejected submission. This stops those paths at the renderer's existing error boundary and rejects unsafe resource ranges, incomplete framebuffers and conflicting compute image imports.

merged.title: fix(port): no more sound gaps on Windows, OpenGL programs kept, Vulkan by default
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
## Before

On Windows the sound cut out in short, ugly gaps. SDL's WASAPI device asks for sound every 10 ms
and our callback rendered the whole sound engine right then, under the same lock the game's
thread takes for every sound call. A wait longer than the device's slack (the game's thread
preempted while holding the lock, the CPU busy while the graphics driver compiles) was a gap.

Every level load also built all OpenGL programs again from the same sources (16 with Enhanced
off), and every run built them once more. That is a compile at the start of each level while the
game already runs.

## After

- The sound is mixed 20 ms ahead of the device on its own thread (Windows, Linux, macOS; Android
  unchanged). SDL's thread only copies from a lock-free ring.
- Game logic sees the same sound timing as before: a sound that ended in frames not heard yet
  still counts as playing, and a stream's time left (the music crossfade) counts those frames.
  Only what you hear is ~20 ms later.
- Gaps

merged.title: fix(enhanced): require reciprocal clearance for medial paths
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
PAL level 11's enhanced-lighting bake can fail with `invalid medial field connection in room 0 (swimming true)`. The same clearance query returns blocked in one direction and clear in the other, while the medial skeleton stores undirected edges. A later traversal then encounters an edge it cannot validate.

The padded body/head rays now check both directions. Near-ray bias can hide an obstacle immediately beside the reverse ray's origin, so either direction's occlusion must reject the connection. Player height, ray bias, endpoint overlap, and the fatal invalid-edge guard are unchanged.

Fixes #173.

Validation:
- Reproduced the reported failure with the bundled 0.10.0 baker and an unmodified PAL level export.
- Added synthetic endpoint-obstacle coverage for walking and swimming: both reverse-direction checks fail before the fix and pass afterward. The test uses no game assets.
- The full level 11 bake completes and verifies all 254 dense grids with the original default traversal settin

merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
Crash reports gain a chronological CPU activity timeline, with separate 32-entry main/game and render trails. Events cover level program/scenery loading, render handoff, scene upload, depth, shadows, lighting, world/effects/HUD and post-processing. Render snapshot indices use `frame=`, game-vsync counters use `tick=`, and loads use `level=` so independent counters cannot be confused.

Messages are copied into fixed storage and truncated to 63 bytes. Recording and snapshotting allocate nothing and never wait: busy slots are skipped. merged.title: perf(port): reduce Vulkan CI setup and scheduling costs
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
Vulkan CI repeats its most expensive image matrices on Fedora and spends substantial time rebuilding compatible test scenes. Keep the complete Vulkan and bake suite in the enhanced job, run a representative Vulkan smoke set plus all non-Vulkan tests on Fedora, and reduce setup and scheduling overhead without changing shaders or comparison tolerances.

- Balance equivalence shards by enum-keyed measured costs, with a positive fallback for new entries. Every registry entry, scenario, enhanced/compatibility mode, determinism check and discarded-attachment comparison remains.
- Reuse compatible GTAO scene setup across quality runs. Retain all six quality runs, 18 contact-pixel cases, MSAA, borrowed-depth, temporal-independence and shader-variant comparisons.
- Allow selected image tests to overlap with bounded Mesa workers; reserve both CI slots for the heavy probe/GTAO/horizon/scrolling matrices. Preserve private cold backend caches and deliberate cache overrides.
- Report phase wall time

opened.author: mateuszklysz
opened.untrustedBody:
A call through a place of a folded wrapper used the call site's type. The runtime resolves the wrapper to the function it calls, whose type hostgen does not know. opened.title: fix(port): no more sound gaps on Windows, OpenGL programs kept, Vulkan by default
opened.author: mateuszklysz
opened.untrustedBody:
## Before

On Windows the sound cut out in short, ugly gaps. SDL's WASAPI device asks for sound every 10 ms
and our callback rendered the whole sound engine right then, under the same lock the game's
thread takes for every sound call. A wait longer than the device's slack (the game's thread
preempted while holding the lock, the CPU busy while the graphics driver compiles) was a gap.

Every level load also built all OpenGL programs again from the same sources (16 with Enhanced
off), and every run built them once more. That is a compile at the start of each level while the
game already runs.

## After

- The sound is mixed 20 ms ahead of the device on its own thread (Windows, Linux, macOS; Android
  unchanged). SDL's thread only copies from a lock-free ring.
- Game logic sees the same sound timing as before: a sound that ended in frames not heard yet
  still counts as playing, and a stream's time left (the music crossfade) counts those frames.
  Only what you hear is ~20 ms later.
- Gaps

merged.title: feat(index): Discord alert when publishing fails, and when it works again
merged.author: Lynder063
merged.untrustedBody:
A failed publish now pings the maintainers' Discord once (with the index-broken issue), and the next good publish closes the issue and says so; without the DISCORD_WEBHOOK_MAINTAINERS secret it stays silent.

opened.title: [WIP] feat(multiplayer): co-op round 3, crossplay, saves, takeover and mod codes
opened.author: Veradictus
opened.untrustedBody:
Round 3 of the RAC1 co-op. Draft: not ready for review or merge.

Adds PAL and NTSC players in one party, co-op saves that never write a player's own story saves, shared progress, every weapon's shots, name tags, late join with Go to host, death rules and optional revive, kick and bans per co-op save, data pack checks, shared camera scripts, enemy grabs, reconnect and host takeover, and mod sync codes.

Reasoning and the settled calls are in `multiplayer/DECISIONS.md`; behaviour and limits are in `multiplayer/README.md`.

Merge together, in this order: this set after #160, then release SDK 1.12, pin `sdk.lock`, tag the mods, deploy the Server (port 7771 is new).

## Tested

Real game on a Mac, hidden clients, local server, 20 of 24 scenario runs passed: join, crates, saves, late join, host loss and name tags, on PAL with PAL and on mixed discs. opened.title: [WIP] feat(item-randomizer): version 2, rebuilt logic and rewards
opened.author: Veradictus
opened.untrustedBody:
Item randomizer 2.0.0. Draft: not ready for review or merge.

Rebuilds the logic from the game's own text and fixes softlocks, wrong banners, lost rewards and Orxon skipping Clank's part. Seed codes move to format 2, so old codes no longer reproduce.

Stacked on the multiplayer draft, which it needs for party play. Retarget to `master` once that merges. The two hook points it needs are in the OpenRAC draft of the same branch name.

## Tested

- 5,760,000 placements swept, all beatable. That run predates the banner commits, which did not touch placement.
- Short real-game runs on both discs: rewards and banners. The vendor purchase, Orxon and lost-reward runs were PAL only.

## Open

- Real NPC scenes played by hand.
- A real two-player party with the randomizer on.
- Challenge mode.
- Archipelago 2.2.0 has the Orxon rule and banners, tested with mocks only; play it for real.
- CI stays red until OpenRAC #166/#167 merge and `sdk-v1.12.0` is pinned in `sdk.lock`.
